qa.q: What qualities should a leader have?
qa.a: Ah well that's a really culturally and context specific thing to be honest. What works for leaders in one place might not work in another. However I feel like a willingness to wield power and take action are large the universal. In addition to being able to inspire others to follow them, a leader's no good without any of those things.

qa.q: Do you think everyone can become team leaders?
qa.a: I mean anyone could be a team leader just by declaring that they are but whether they are an effective one or not is another matter entirely. We all know people who are managers but are pretty ineffective.

qa.q: Why do some people dislike teamwork?
qa.a: Well in a group of people there will be those who are more productive than others and some more productive people might resent it if they get an equal share of recognition or pay when they did most of the work. Other people just really dislike coming to consensus with others and like to go their own way since they feel it's more effective.

qa.q: Do you think young people are good team players?
qa.a: I mean they could be if they have a natural disposition towards that. I suppose though it's not something everyone has and they might have to learn it. It's important to remember in these cases that people are individuals so I prefer to avoid sweeping statements of agreement about that sort of thing.

qa.q: What are the benefits and drawbacks of working in a team?
qa.a: Well there are probably as many of one as there are of the other. You have the advantages of pooled resources and distributed responsibility so you should theoretically be able to do more and if you fail then it's no one person's fault. As for the downsides beyond the ones I mentioned when we talked about why people dislike it, I'm really not sure. Maybe having to tolerate other people if you're not a social person might be a downside but I don't know for sure.

qa.q: How can a team deal with conflicts among its members?
qa.a: Well breaking up the team might be the ultimate solution. No team, no conflict. Before letting it get to that extreme though it could be a good idea to pursue mediation or attempt some kind of collective agreement everyone can get on board with so the team functions on agreed terms.

qa.q: How do cultural differences affect team dynamics?
qa.a: I suppose they could be beneficial in that you might get different perspectives and approaches to problems that monoculture might not allow for but that could be a double-edged sword if everyone or if not everyone agrees on the best practices or approaches.

qa.q: How do team sports and group projects in school prepare young people for working in teams late in life?
